provenance.note: Archival compilation - the legacy primary_source (Nagendra, Nature in the City, OUP 2016) / secondary_sources keys and per-record notes carry the citations. Conservative V0: only named cases with unambiguous documented conversion; see summary._estimate_notes for the ~280-kere gazetteer context.

summary._estimate_notes: Conservative inventory based on Nagendra (OUP 2016), Fathima Samana (2008), Ramachandra IISc CES surveys, and Citizen Matters reporting. Greater Bengaluru has ~280 historical kere documented in 19th-century gazetteers vs. ~70-100 functional today, so 'fully lost' likely runs into the dozens at the BBMP scale - this V0 lists only the named cases where conversion to built use is unambiguously documented by name.

primary_source.name: Harini Nagendra, Nature in the City: Bengaluru in the Past, Present, and Future (Oxford University Press 2016)

secondary_sources.name: Fathima Samana - Historical Evolution of Tank System in Bangalore City (2008)
T.V. Ramachandra et al. (IISc CES) - Wetlands of Bengaluru 105-lake survey

lost_bodies.name: Dharmambudhi tank
lost_bodies.note: Kempegowda-era kere (mid-16th century), Kempegowda's second tank after Kempambudhi. Drained in the 1950s for the construction of Kempegowda Bus Station (Majestic). The bus stand itself bears Kempegowda's name; the kere that surrounded it does not.

lost_bodies.name: Sampangi tank
lost_bodies.note: Gave its name to Sampangi Tank Road and the Sampangiramnagar neighbourhood. Built over for the Sri Kanteerava Indoor and Outdoor stadiums. The hockey-stadium and aquatic-stadium complex now occupy the original tank bed.

lost_bodies.name: Karanji Anjaneya tank
lost_bodies.note: Tank bed redeveloped into the Bishop Cotton Boys School playing fields and the surrounding Richmond Road education campus.

lost_bodies.name: Akkithimmanahalli tank
lost_bodies.note: Converted into a hockey stadium (Akkithimmanahalli Hockey Stadium) in central Bengaluru. The stadium still uses the tank's name; the water does not.

lost_bodies.name: Domlur tank
lost_bodies.note: Drained for the BDA Domlur Layout and associated arterial road network east of MG Road.

lost_bodies.name: Kempambudhi tank
lost_bodies.note: Kempegowda's family-deity tank, ~1550s. Survives in name and in a much-reduced footprint but is heavily sewage-contaminated; INTACH has documented its degradation. The structure remains, but as a sewage-receiving body, not a kere.

lost_bodies.name: Halsoor (Ulsoor) Lake
lost_bodies.note: Survives at 38 hectares per OSM but is a fraction of its 19th-century pre-Cantonment extent. The 1811 cantonment garrison was laid out around it; subsequent road and rail encroachment cut into the original tank perimeter and storm drains.

lost_bodies.name: Sankey Tank
lost_bodies.note: Named after Col Richard Hieram Sankey (British military engineer who designed it in 1882). Survives as a decorative water body in central Malleshwaram but its original cascade connections are gone.

lost_bodies.name: Bellandur Lake
lost_bodies.note: Survives at 317 hectares - the largest kere in BBMP - but functionally degraded: receives ~400-500 MLD of untreated sewage daily, caught fire in May 2015 (foam-fire), February 2018 (30+ hour fire), and 2021. Forward Foundation v State of Karnataka (NGT 2018) ordered Rs 500 crore for revival; fires have subsided but sewage load has not.
